questions.question: First apply reorder_dimensions(dimension_order=[size, revenue_usd, base_price_usd, discount_percent, final_price_usd, units_sold]). With size next to revenue_usd, do polylines suggest that bigger normalized sizes line up with higher revenue, or is the bundle messy? Describe only what you can see from line crossings and density.

answer.value: Putting size beside revenue shows a very loose coupling: across the normalized polylines the Pearson correlation between size and revenue is essentially zero, and the bundle is full of crossings rather than a clean band. Some large-size shoes still sit on modest revenue and vice versa, so “bigger product” does not read as a simple recipe for higher revenue in this view.

key_insights: Size and revenue move largely independently—no strong diagonal bundle between those two axes.
Discount and units_sold axes add more spread, which is why the lines look tangled rather than stratified.

reasoning.reasoning: Brings size and revenue adjacent so their joint pattern is readable along each product polyline.
